title: Shapley Value-driven Data Pruning for Recommender Systems

problem.claim: Recommender systems suffer from noisy interactions, including accidental clicks and popularity bias.

gap.claim: Existing denoising methods can overlook the training value of interactions classified as noisy and retain clean interactions with little learning value because they rely on assumed user intent.

contributions.claim: SVV evaluates interactions according to their objective impact on model training rather than subjective intent assumptions.
SVV uses real-time Shapley value estimation to quantify each interaction's contribution to reducing training loss.
The work develops a simulated noise protocol for systematic examination of denoising approaches.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four real-world datasets report that SVV outperforms existing denoising methods in accuracy and robustness.
Further analysis reports that SVV preserves training-critical interactions and provides interpretable noise assessment.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recommender systems face noisy interactions such as accidental clicks and popularity bias.
Intent-based denoising may discard useful interactions and retain low-value ones.
SVV values interactions using model-training impact and real-time Shapley estimation.
The framework emphasizes high-value interactions, downplays low-value ones, and includes a simulated noise protocol.
Reported experiments and analysis indicate gains in accuracy, robustness, preservation of critical interactions, and interpretability.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the four datasets, baselines, metrics, or numerical effect sizes.
The abstract does not specify the computational cost, approximation details, or deployment constraints of real-time Shapley estimation.
The abstract does not describe the simulated noise protocol or its relationship to naturally occurring noise.
